# Epic: Pre-surfacing reviewer-findings verifier agent (F4 + F5 bundle)

## Context

DSO maintainers and autonomous-resolution sub-agents currently consume reviewer findings — including invalid ones — without any pre-surfacing verification step. PR-80 saw 8 of 11 round-2 findings invalid; PR #102 had 3 verified hallucinations claiming "undefined function" on functions defined at lines 94/108 of the same file; PR #103 cycled 19→33→17 findings with ~0% line-overlap. Invalid findings consume autonomous-resolution attempts (CLAUDE.md rule 11; default 5 attempts each), introduce unnecessary complexity into the codebase when acted upon, and erode trust in the review pipeline. The existing `code-reviewer-arbiter` is a post-defense dispute adjudicator invoked only on `ESCALATE_REVIEW` or `oscillation_no_arbiter_engagement` — it cannot catch these failure modes because invalid findings reach the PR untouched and burn resolution attempts before any defense escalates.

## Approach

This epic bundles two related fixes from the post-PR-#103 calibration analysis: F4 (structured `verification_evidence` schema field) and F5 (verifier sub-agent that consumes it). F5 needs F4 to function on absence claims, so they ship together.

**F4 — Schema extension and reviewer-prompt updates.** Extend the existing reviewer-findings schema (which already carries `cited_excerpt`, shipped at commit 729d2c2075) with a sibling field `verification_evidence: {command, output}`. When a reviewer finding makes an absence claim, the reviewer captures the grep/stat/path-resolve command plus its output as proof. Update all 10 existing `code-reviewer-*` agent files (light, standard, performance, deep-arch, deep-correctness, deep-hygiene, deep-verification, security-red-team, security-blue-team, test-quality) to emit this field. Absence-language detection uses an expanded synonym anchor list at the schema-validation boundary: canonical triggers (undefined / missing / does not exist / not defined / not found) plus reviewer-rephrasing variants (unable to locate / appears to be absent / no implementation / no definition visible / cannot find / cannot be found / has no corresponding / has no definition / no [X] visible / is called but [no/has no]). Empirical probe (this brainstorm session) showed reviewer LLMs gravitate to canonical triggers in practice, so the anchor list catches the realistic failure mode without a semantic-classifier fallback.

**F5 — Verifier sub-agent.** Build a new `code-reviewer-verifier` sub-agent dispatched between every reviewer and `record-review.sh` in both the CI llm-review path (`plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/runner.py`) and the local `/dso:review` path (REVIEW-WORKFLOW reviewer dispatch). The verifier runs against critical/important/fragile findings only (minor findings pass through unverified). For each in-scope finding, the verifier inspects the cited file (read at the snapshot SHA, not live filesystem) and the F4 `verification_evidence` payload, then emits one of three rulings:

- `confirm` — claim is verifiably true; finding enters the autonomous-resolution loop unchanged.
- `downgrade-to-minor` — claim is true but reachability, scope, or severity is wrong; finding becomes a normal minor PR comment (no resolution attempt).
- `drop` — claim is verifiably false; finding is removed before reaching the PR or resolution loop.

Rubric: defer to the original reviewer on uncertainty (the verifier never drops a finding on insufficient evidence — it confirms and lets the existing autonomous-resolution loop handle it). Empirical probe (this brainstorm session) confirmed sonnet does NOT systematically over-confirm under this rubric on clear contradictions — drop rate was 3/3 on the PR-#102 hallucination class (Test 1) and 3/3 on an authoritatively-toned variant (Test 2). The rubric correctly defers (1 confirm, 2 downgrade, 0 drop) on a genuinely-ambiguous case (Test 3 — definition exists in a sibling file).

**Snapshot SHA anchor.** The reviewer's dispatch wrapper captures `<reviewed_sha>` at reviewer-dispatch time. Both reviewer and verifier operate against this SHA. The local verifier reads files via `git show <reviewed_sha>:<path>`; the CI verifier's pre-packaged file contents are extracted from `<reviewed_sha>` (not the working tree, not the verifier-dispatch-time SHA). Mid-review commits cannot shift the verifier's view.

**Independent verification_evidence re-execution (CI).** The CI dispatch wrapper re-executes the reviewer's stated `verification_evidence.command` against `<reviewed_sha>` (sandboxed: read-only allowlist, no network). The captured output is compared against `verification_evidence.output`. On mismatch, the verifier receives an `evidence_invalidated: true` flag in its prompt; the verifier treats invalidated evidence as positive contradiction, favoring `drop` when the original claim depended on it. This closes the "hallucinated grep output" loophole — a fabricated reviewer evidence command produces no matching output and flips the verifier's input.

**Asymmetric tool access.** The CI verifier is an LLM API call with file contents and re-executed evidence pre-packaged into the prompt by the dispatch wrapper (no Bash, no Read at runtime). The local verifier is a Claude Code sub-agent with `Read`, `Glob`, and a bounded `Bash` allowlist (`grep`, `stat`, `ls`, `file` — no writes, no network). Both paths use the sonnet tier and a path-aware prompt template that explicitly distinguishes "context is complete" (CI: pre-packaged) from "context is live-readable" (local).

Each ruling carries a `file:line-region` fingerprint. Schema enforces `<path>:<line-start>-<line-end>` with `line-start == line-end` for single-line findings (no `path:120` shorthand). This shape is the stable matching surface for a future cross-cycle convergence matcher (F7b).

**Feature flag.** Config key `review.verifier_enabled` (default `false`). Verifier dispatch is wrapped in a flag check at both CI and local entry points. When disabled, the pipeline behaves identically to the pre-epic state. Per-project opt-in after fixture validation. The dispatch wrapper itself catches all exceptions and treats wrapper-side crashes as `verifier_status: failed` — never blocks `record-review.sh`.

**Coordinated rollout.** Schema validation of `verification_evidence` operates in two phases. (1) Soft-deprecation window: missing field on absence-tagged findings logs a warning to review output but does not reject. (2) Hard enforcement: activates only when the consuming project's plugin cache has BOTH the F4 schema and the 10 updated reviewer agents present (detected by version-marker file shipped by the plugin). Window length: configurable via `review.verifier_strict_after` (default: 2 minor plugin releases after F4 ships).

**Failure handling.** Any verifier failure (timeout, malformed output, MAX_AGENTS=0, sub-agent unavailable, API error, dispatch wrapper crash) annotates the finding with `verifier_status: failed` and passes it through unchanged (fail-open). Per-review failure-rate threshold (`review.verifier_failure_threshold`, default 0.30) escalates the entire review to user attention. Threshold range bounds: validation rejects values outside `(0.0, 1.0]`. **Cascading-failure brake**: when failure rate exceeds the threshold AND in-scope-finding count ≥ 5, the autonomous-resolution loop is also paused for the failing findings (CLAUDE.md rule 11 attempt counter held), preventing pre-epic invalid-finding pipeline restoration under sustained CI degradation.

**Telemetry.** Per-review confirm/downgrade-to-minor/drop counts, verifier-failure rate, fingerprint emissions, and minor-finding rate (canary for severity-undergrading regression) surface in (a) per-review output (PR comment in CI, terminal output locally) and (b) `review-stats` aggregations alongside existing reviewer-tier and resolution-rate metrics.

**Regression fixture corpus** (verifier-specific; distinct from the general reviewer rubric corpus owned by epic a72d-df57) built from open bug tickets `ee3a-43fc-652b-49ff` (PR #102 hallucinated "undefined function"), `b2ef-cd72-76b1-4f01` (PR #100 invalid critical findings + severity-inflated important), `9e84-2b78-c2ce-426b` (PR-#102 false-positive trust-boundary on .coderabbit.yaml). Corpus replayed at sprint close in **both** CI and local paths to verify ruling behavior AND cross-path equivalence (≥95% identical rulings required). Includes: a known-ambiguous case (asserts the defer-rubric ruling), a known-fabricated-evidence case (asserts CI re-execution flips to `drop`), and a known-rephrased absence claim using non-canonical wording (asserts F4 expanded-synonym anchor catches it).

**Governance — rule 11 exception.** ADR `docs/adr/0013-verifier-severity-authority.md` (drafted during this brainstorm) documents that the `code-reviewer-verifier` sub-agent's `downgrade-to-minor` and `drop` rulings are an explicit, narrowly-scoped exception to CLAUDE.md rule 11 (no severity overrides in `runner.py`). The exception is gated on (1) sub-agent identity, (2) ruling enum, (3) documented dispatch surface, and (4) `review.verifier_enabled=true`. The implementation work for this epic is limited to updating CLAUDE.md rule 11 to add the one-sentence cross-reference pointing to the ADR — the ADR text itself is already in the repo.

## Success Criteria

1. Reviewer-findings schema extends `cited_excerpt` with a sibling `verification_evidence: {command: string, output: string}` field. Schema validation requires `verification_evidence` on every finding whose claim text matches the absence-language pattern set (canonical + expanded reviewer-rephrasing variants per Approach). Enforcement applies in both CI llm-review and local `/dso:review` paths. Validation runs in soft-deprecation mode initially per `review.verifier_strict_after`; hard rejection requires both F4 schema and the 10 updated reviewer agents present in the plugin cache (version-marker check).

2. All 10 existing `code-reviewer-*` agent files updated to emit `verification_evidence` when their finding cites absence-language; each agent has a behavioral fixture asserting it emits the field on a known absence-claim diff. The 10 agents are updated in a single plugin-cache version bump alongside the schema validator.

3. `code-reviewer-verifier` sub-agent file exists at `plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-verifier.md`. Ruling shape: `{finding_id, ruling: confirm|downgrade-to-minor|drop, fingerprint: "<path>:<line-start>-<line-end>" (line-start == line-end on single-line findings), verifier_status: ok|failed, evidence_invalidated: bool, rationale}`. Schema validated at the verifier output boundary.

4. CI dispatch wrapper in `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/runner.py` calls the verifier between reviewer dispatch and `plugins/dso/hooks/record-review.sh` for each critical/important/fragile finding. Wrapper pre-packages the cited file contents (extracted from `<reviewed_sha>`, not live filesystem), the `verification_evidence` payload, and a re-executed-evidence comparison result. Minor findings bypass the verifier.

5. Local `/dso:review` reviewer pipeline dispatches the verifier as a Claude Code sub-agent with `Read`, `Glob`, and bounded `Bash` allowlist (`grep`, `stat`, `ls`, `file`). The verifier reads files via `git show <reviewed_sha>:<path>` (not the live working tree). Minor findings bypass the verifier.

6. Verifier rulings have explicit semantics in the autonomous-resolution loop: `confirm` enters the loop unchanged; `downgrade-to-minor` becomes a normal minor PR comment with no resolution attempt; `drop` removes the finding before any PR-surface or resolution-loop processing.

7. CI dispatch wrapper independently re-executes the reviewer's `verification_evidence.command` against `<reviewed_sha>` (sandboxed: read-only allowlist, no network) and compares output against `verification_evidence.output`. On mismatch, the verifier prompt receives `evidence_invalidated: true`; verifier rules `drop` when the original claim depended on the invalidated evidence. Behavioral fixture: a reviewer-emitted command whose output is fabricated triggers `drop`.

8. Snapshot SHA invariant: `<reviewed_sha>` is captured at reviewer-dispatch time and propagates through reviewer, verifier, record-review.sh, and PR-comment surface. Test asserts that a mid-review commit (push between reviewer and verifier dispatch) does not change the SHA the verifier evaluates against.

9. Verifier failure handling: any failure annotates the finding with `verifier_status: failed` and passes it through unchanged (fail-open). `review.verifier_failure_threshold` (default 0.30, range `(0.0, 1.0]`) — failures above threshold escalate the review to user attention via a distinguishable PR comment label. **Cascading-failure brake**: when threshold exceeded AND in-scope-finding count ≥ 5, autonomous-resolution loop pauses for the failing findings (rule 11 attempt counter held).

10. Per-ruling `file:line-region` fingerprint emitted for every verified finding (confirm or downgrade); shape `<path>:<line-start>-<line-end>` with `line-start == line-end` on single-line findings; validated by schema. Surfaces as a stable matching surface for future F7b convergence work.

11. Telemetry: confirm/downgrade/drop counts, verifier-failure rate, per-finding fingerprints, AND review-level minor-finding rate (severity-undergrading canary) visible in (a) per-review output (PR comment for CI, terminal output for local) and (b) `review-stats` aggregations. The new fields (`verifier_confirm_count`, `verifier_downgrade_count`, `verifier_drop_count`, `verifier_failure_rate`, `verifier_minor_finding_rate`, `verifier_fingerprints[]`) are added to the review-stats schema definition that epic 5df7-63ac (integrated observability) will consume — schema additions are co-coordinated with that epic.

12. Regression fixture corpus (verifier-specific; distinct from a72d-df57's general reviewer rubric corpus) replayed at sprint close in **both** CI and local paths. Required ruling behavior: `drop` on PR-#102 hallucinated "undefined function" (ee3a-43fc); `downgrade-to-minor` on PR-#100 severity-inflated important (b2ef-cd72); `drop` on .coderabbit.yaml false-positive trust-boundary (9e84-2b78); the defer-rubric ruling on the known-ambiguous case; `drop` on the known-fabricated-evidence case (re-execution flips it); `verification_evidence`-required on the known-rephrased absence claim. Cross-path ruling equivalence: ≥95% identical rulings between CI and local paths across the corpus.

13. Feature flag `review.verifier_enabled` (default `false`) gates verifier dispatch at both CI and local entry points. When disabled, pipeline behaves identically to pre-epic state (verified by replaying the corpus with flag off and confirming pre-epic ruling distribution). The dispatch wrapper catches all exceptions and treats wrapper-side crashes as `verifier_status: failed` — never blocks `record-review.sh`.

14. CLAUDE.md rule 11 is updated to add a single sentence at the end of its existing text pointing to `docs/adr/0013-verifier-severity-authority.md` and naming the four-prong exception scope (sub-agent identity, ruling enum, dispatch surface, feature-flag gating). The ADR text itself is already in the repo (drafted during the brainstorm session for this epic).

## Probe Findings (resolved during brainstorm)

Two pre-implementation probes were run during brainstorm to de-risk the rubric and pattern-set design:

**F1 Sycophancy Probe** — 3 test cases × 3 sonnet runs each measuring confirm-bias on clear contradictions under the defer-on-uncertainty rubric.
- Test 1 (clear contradiction, PR-#102 hallucination class): **drop 3/3** — sonnet correctly drops on direct evidence contradiction.
- Test 2 (same contradiction, authoritative reviewer tone): **drop 3/3** — authoritative tone does not bias the verifier toward confirm.
- Test 3 (genuine ambiguity, definition exists in sibling file): **0 drop / 1 confirm / 2 downgrade-to-minor** — verifier handles ambiguity thoughtfully without blanket-deferring.
- **Conclusion**: defer-on-uncertainty rubric is empirically sound under sonnet. The 3-way rubric (`confirm` / `downgrade-to-minor` / `drop`) is retained without need for an explicit `uncertain` ruling.

**F3 Absence-Language Variant Probe** — 8 rephrased absence claims through schema-validator pattern sets + 3 sonnet reviewer outputs on a real missing-function diff.
- Static pattern (canonical triggers only): **6 of 8 variants bypassed** — 75% bypass rate on intentionally-rephrased absence claims.
- Static pattern (expanded triggers — canonical + 13 reviewer-rephrasing variants): **0 of 8 bypassed** — full coverage.
- Reviewer-output collection (3 emissions on a real bug): **3/3 used canonical triggers** ("not defined", "undefined", "missing"). Reviewer LLMs gravitate to canonical phrasing in practice.
- **Conclusion**: expanded synonym anchor is sufficient for the realistic failure mode; haiku-tier semantic-classifier fallback is unnecessary and removed from the spec.

## Scenario Analysis (surviving)

- **Verifier dispatch doubles review latency under load** (`high`, `runtime`) — addressed by feature-flag default-off (SC13) + per-finding parallelization opportunity in dispatch wrapper.
- **Race between verifier file Read and concurrent worktree edits** (`high`, `runtime`) — addressed by snapshot SHA anchor (SC8).
- **CI pre-packaged file contents stale relative to reviewer snapshot** (`high`, `runtime`) — addressed by snapshot SHA anchor (SC8).
- **Absence-language regex false negatives bypass verification_evidence requirement** (`high`, `runtime`) — addressed by expanded synonym anchor (SC1) + Probe Findings F3 (validated empirically).
- **Fail-open on verifier failure restores the pre-epic invalid-finding pipeline** (`high`, `runtime`) — addressed by cascading-failure brake (SC9).
- **Schema validation rejects in-flight reviewer outputs from older agent versions** (`critical`, `deployment`) — addressed by coordinated rollout / version-marker gating (SC1).
- **Verifier agent file missing in plugin cache after partial sync** (`high`, `deployment`) — addressed by feature flag default-off (SC13) + dispatch-wrapper exception catch (SC13).
- **agent-routing.conf collision with concurrent dso-8l5h extraction epic** (`high`, `deployment`) — surfaced as Cross-Epic Interaction (dso-8l5h); deployment-time check in implementation plan.
- **CI llm-review job lacks rollback path when verifier hard-fails** (`critical`, `deployment`) — addressed by feature flag (SC13) + wrapper exception catch (SC13).
- **Bounded Bash allowlist blocks legitimate verification on grep-incompatible filesystems** (`medium`, `configuration`) — accepted; `git show <SHA>:<path>` reads do not require the allowlist on those platforms.
- **Fingerprint shape ambiguous for single-line findings** (`medium`, `configuration`) — addressed by schema constraint `line-start == line-end` (SC3, SC10).
- **Minor findings bypass verifier — severity-undergrading attack** (`medium`, `configuration`) — addressed by minor-finding-rate canary in telemetry (SC11).
- **Hallucinated `verification_evidence`** (`critical`, `assumption`) — addressed by independent CI re-execution + `evidence_invalidated` flag (SC7).
- **Defer-to-reviewer-on-uncertainty inverts cost model** (`high`, `assumption`) — **REJECTED by Probe F1** — empirically the rubric works correctly; sonnet does not over-confirm on clear contradictions.
- **Critical/important/fragile classification reliability** (`high`, `assumption`) — partially addressed by minor-finding-rate canary (SC11); residual risk accepted.
- **CI verifier and local verifier produce equivalent rulings** (`high`, `assumption`) — addressed by cross-path ruling equivalence SC (SC12).
- **Rule 11 governance handwave** (`medium`, `assumption`) — addressed by ADR + rule 11 update (SC14).

## Prompt Alignment Findings (resolved)

- **Matched signal**: agent definitions (new `code-reviewer-verifier` agent + 10 updated `code-reviewer-*` agents).
- **Bot-psych F1 — Over-confirm sycophancy**: Probe F1 ran during brainstorm — hypothesis NOT confirmed. Sonnet correctly drops on clear contradictions (3/3 in two test cases). Defer-on-uncertainty rubric retained.
- **Bot-psych F2 — CI vs. local prompt-template divergence**: addressed by path-aware prompt template (Approach) + cross-path ruling-equivalence fixture (SC12).
- **Bot-psych F3 — Absence-language pattern evasion**: Probe F3 ran during brainstorm — partially confirmed (75% bypass on rephrased variants for canonical pattern; 0% bypass for expanded pattern; reviewer LLMs use canonical in practice). Expanded synonym anchor adopted (SC1); semantic-classifier fallback rejected as unnecessary.
- **Bot-psych F4 — Failure-threshold volume-sensitivity**: addressed by cascading-failure brake (SC9) — threshold drives an actionable consequence (resolution-loop pause), not just a label.

## Dependencies

- `cited_excerpt` schema field is shipped (commit 729d2c2075). F4 extension is in scope of this epic, not a prerequisite.
- ample-seize-siege (677d-a6a0-0c2e-4b9e) — closed.
- No other blocking dependencies.

  Constraint: forward-declare verifier schema additions in distributed schema; reserve schema-version migration strategy.

  Constraint: define verifier telemetry fields in unified telemetry schema before emission.

  Constraint: ensure verifier dispatch is replicated per-worktree and remains sandwiched between reviewer and record-review.sh.

  Constraint: verifier ruling output compatible with closure-checks schema modifications.

  Overlapping epic: a72d-df57 — Reviewer rubric replay corpus

Sprint ordering preference: this epic ships before a72d-df57 builds its general corpus, so the corpus targets the v2 schema.

  Constraint: use `review.verifier_*` prefix (`review.verifier_enabled`, `review.verifier_failure_threshold`, `review.verifier_strict_after`).

  Overlapping epic: dso-8l5h — Extract review and evaluation sub-agents
  Constraint: align verifier agent file naming with dso-8l5h extraction pattern; coordinate agent-routing.conf registration; deployment-time check in implementation plan asserts verifier registration succeeded.

- Resource: review overlay agent dispatch framework
  Overlapping epic: dso-q0lo — Prevent the explosion of documentation created by LLMs (code-reviewer-doc overlay)
  Constraint: clarify overlay agent ordering; ensure classifier output schema supports both overlay dispatch signals.

- Resource: code review finding volume / quality signals in review-stats
  Overlapping epic: e22e-b7a2 — Implementation reliability
  Constraint: track verifier drop/downgrade actions separately in review-stats so improvements and verifier filtering do not conflate.

- Resource: reviewer-findings + severity classification semantics (umbrella calibration epic)
  Overlapping epic: e7f3-2b45 (grainy-speck-ball) — Code review calibration umbrella
  Constraint: this epic is one of four calibration fixes (F4+F5 here, F6 shipped PR #106, F7b separate epic TBD).

- Resource: plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/runner.py
  Overlapping epic: f9f8-a15c — Add Gemini provider to CI LLM review provider abstraction
  Constraint: position verifier dispatch after provider selection but before record-review.sh call.

- Resource: review-findings schema + resolution-loop entry mechanics
  Overlapping epic: jira-dig-1673 — Reviewer override discipline
  Constraint: verifier `drop` ruling prevents findings from reaching override-discipline gate entirely; clarify whether `downgrade-to-minor` findings can still trigger override-discipline.
